I investigated this a little bit and noticed something interesting; while remote debugging with chrome and 
android (chrome 56, Android 7) I noticed that when you enter in values via the remote debugging window it works 100% fine but as mentioned when you use the mobiles keyboard it will not behave the same and only update on end of word. 
I also tested with ReactiveForms and works totally fine there https://plnkr.co/edit/3EtveUEwS6Q7X757N2Oz?p=preview

Went a bit deeper (thanks @Toxicable for helping out) - it's related to https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/c5ea03a023ccece0c55158ac274e9f9aa7b47e1e

Maybe @vthinkxie can comment? I think we should maybe listen to the `compositionupdate` event as well, but I don't have enough experience to know for sure. @robdodson any advice here? 

(for those wanting to replicate, on OS X you can turn on the japanese Hiritanga/Katakana keyboard and see this behavior) - see also https://jsfiddle.net/oamnkkvL/ for seeing what happens on different setups

Also, the fact this works with reactive forms means we probably have a mismatch in our API

Well, it sounds like you already confirmed that this is definitely an Angular problem, so not sure if this is helpful, but I was just testing your suggestions and replying when your last comments popped up.

---

re: Chrome, nope, it's definitely not a Chrome / Android / Google Keyboard issue; Cyph still works as expected for me in prod.

re: Zone.js, just tested both `assertInAngularZone` and `zone.run` (and also tried reverting from Zone.js 0.8.0 to the version we have in prod, 0.7.6), and nothing changed.

Also, I was able to reproduce @Toxicable's observation that his `ReactiveFormsModule` variant of the Plunker doesn't have the same problem.

@robwormald It seems that android device has different behavior with pc when you enter english words.

listen to the compositionupdate event will cause bugs when user input in Chinese|Korea|Japanese typing mode.

In [angularjs code](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/a24777a2c4ad2ac087d9e3aa278fa2e61e8cc740/src/ng/directive/input.js#L1240), when android device is detected the composition event listener should be disabled. 

I think this can be patched as well in Angular 4.x code, then I find that there is a UA detector in [exist code](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/bebedfed24d6fbfa492e97f071e1d1b41e411280/packages/platform-browser/testing/src/browser_util.ts#L30), but it seems that these code is only used for testing.

Any one has idea to patch this to forms module?

issue.title: fix(forms): make composition event buffering configurable

labels.name: action: merge
labels.description: The PR is ready for merge by the caretaker

issue.body:
This commit fixes a regression where `ngModel` no longer syncs letter by letter on Android devices, and instead syncs at the end of every word. This broke when we introduced buffering of IME events so IMEs like Pinyin keyboards or Katakana keyboards wouldn't display composition strings. Unfortunately, iOS devices and Android devices have opposite event behavior. Whereas iOS devices fire composition events for IME keyboards only, Android fires composition events for Latin-language keyboards. For this reason, languages like English don't work as expected on Android if we always buffer. So to support both platforms, composition string buffering will only be turned on by default for non-Android devices.

However, we have also added a `COMPOSITION_BUFFER_MODE` token to make this configurable by the application, because in some cases, apps might might still want to receive intermediate values. For example, some inputs begin searching behavior based on Latin letters before a character selection is made.

As a provider, this is fairly flexible. If you want to turn composition buffering off, simply provide the token at the top level:

```ts
providers: [
   {provide: COMPOSITION_BUFFER_MODE, useValue: false}
]
```

Or, if you want to change the mode  based on locale or platform, you can use a factory:

```ts
import {shouldUseBuffering} from 'my/lib';

....
providers: [
   {provide: COMPOSITION_BUFFER_MODE, useFactory: shouldUseBuffering}
]
```

Closes #15079.
